page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the configuration supplies 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated virtual CPUs with hyperthreading enabled. Compute resources are coupled with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. The processor architecture includes 33 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX and AVX-512F instruction sets. The server includes no bundled local storage and provision zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes and external networking attachments.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced multi-threaded compute alongside average memory throughput. The server attained a PassMark CPU score of 10,041.11 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 8,825.18, aligning with median results for its core tier. In-memory execution demonstrated solid throughput, reaching 11.0 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and an uncached memory read bandwidth of 60.77 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing remains limited, as shown by a weak stress-ng single-core score of 1,109.08 and modest compression throughput under gzip and bzip3 routines.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides effective cost efficiency for environments needing ample memory allocation without paying for excess compute cores. Because it features dedicated CPU allocation but lacks local disks, primary tradeoffs involve dependency on remote network block storage latency and sub-optimal performance for single-threaded batch computing. The instance is suited for in-memory caches like Redis, mid-tier relational database hosting, memory-heavy microservices, and general data buffering pipelines.
